name: Mateo Haddad
headline: Security Engineer
summary: Security engineer focused on securing application and platform code, reducing risk in production systems, and partnering with engineering teams on practical controls. Comfortable working across cloud environments and low-level services, with a strong bias toward measurable improvements and maintainable fixes.

roles.title: Junior Security Engineer
bullets: Supported secure delivery on Agile teams by reviewing changes in Azure and advising engineers on safer implementation patterns.
Built internal hardening tools in Go and Rust that reduced repeated manual checks by 30%.
Investigated risky code paths and helped close 18 security issues before release, improving consistency across the backend.
Created lightweight guidance for developers that translated review findings into clearer repair steps.

roles.title: Application Security Engineer
bullets: Strengthened application controls in Azure by adding checks around OAuth flows and reducing authorization defects by 25%.
Worked with developers on C++ services to remove unsafe patterns and improve error handling in user-facing features.
Reviewed design changes on Agile projects and aligned fixes with the security team’s release priorities.
Traced recurring account-access issues to weak integration logic and helped stabilize the affected service.

roles.title: Software Engineer
bullets: Developed backend components in AWS using C, C++ and Cryptography to protect sensitive data in transit and at rest.
Implemented IAM and OAuth safeguards for internal platforms, cutting privileged-access exceptions by 40%.
Improved service resilience by tightening key handling and reducing security-related incidents across shared infrastructure.
Partnered with product and operations teams to roll out controls without slowing delivery.

projects.name: Echo Router
projects.description: Built Echo Router in C, Go and Rust to route internal traffic through a compact, security-focused service layer. The project emphasized predictable behavior, clean boundaries and safer handling of messages between components.
